title: Minimal Polynomial vs Characteristic Polynomial of Matrices
description: Formalizes the fundamental relationship between minimal and characteristic polynomials of matrices: minpoly K M divides charpoly M, both are monic, minpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton variant), and roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The minimal polynomial of a matrix M over a field K is the monic polynomial of smallest degree that annihilates M. The Cayley-Hamilton theorem states charpoly(M) annihilates M. It follows that minpoly(M) | charpoly(M). Both are monic, and the eigenvalues (roots of charpoly) are also roots of minpoly.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) minpoly K M divides charpoly M. (2) Both are monic. (3) charpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton). (4) minpoly degree ≤ dim(M). (5) Roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly.
overview.proofStrategy: Most results follow from Mathlib's minpoly and charpoly APIs. minpoly_dvd_charpoly: use minpoly.dvd and charpoly_monic. charpoly_annihilates: Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly. minpoly_annihilates: minpoly.aeval.
keyInsights: **Divisibility**: minpoly(M) | charpoly(M) because charpoly(M)[M] = 0 (Cayley-Hamilton) and minpoly(M) divides any annihilating polynomial.
**Degree bounds**: deg(minpoly) ≤ n = dim(K^n) since the n+1 matrices {I, M, M², ..., M^n} are linearly dependent in Mat_n(K).
**Root relationship**: Every root of minpoly is a root of charpoly (divisibility). The converse may fail (Jordan blocks).
**Cayley-Hamilton**: charpoly(M)(M) = 0 — the matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial.

sections.mathContext: Every root of $\text{charpoly}(M)$ is a root of $\text{minpoly}(M)$, and vice versa.

conclusion.summary: Minpoly-charpoly relationship fully formalized: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Divisibility, annihilation, degree bounds, and root relationships all proved.
conclusion.implications: This provides the core infrastructure for Jordan normal form theory in Lean 4. The minpoly | charpoly relationship is fundamental to understanding diagonalizability (minpoly splits into distinct linear factors) vs. Jordan decomposition.
openQuestions: Can the Jordan normal form theorem be formalized in Lean 4 using this infrastructure?
Can the characterization of diagonalizable matrices (minpoly has no repeated roots) be proved?
Can the rational canonical form (based on minpoly factorization) be formalized?
